pray verb

also say one’s prayers, praying, let us pray

classical

Verg. A. 9.24: multa deōs ōrāns (Lewis & Short)
Vulg. Lc. 11.1
M-O s.v. pray (religious)

ōrō, ōrāre, ōrāvī, ōrātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Classically to beg, beseech, the gods among others; used absolutely, “to pray”, in the Vulgate and the Church (Lewis & Short). Ōrēmus, let us pray; ōrāre prō aliquō, to pray for someone.

Other words

  • precor, precārī, precātus sum — pray, entreat (a god)

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. ND 1.119: deōs colere, precārī, venerārīque (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Cicero’s verb for praying to the gods; the school dialogues use it for saying one’s prayers (precātus es Deum?, Corderius).

Examples

  • Domine, docē nōs ōrāre

    Lord, teach us to prayVulg. Lc. 11.1

  • Prius ōrēmus.

    Let’s pray first (before the meal, or before getting up from it).Schott. Conf., Convīvium nundinārium

  • An precātus es Deum? — Cum prīmum frāter mē pexuit, precātus sum.

    Have you said your prayers? — As soon as my brother had combed my hair, I said them.Cord. Coll. 1.2

See also prayer, kneel, the Lord’s Prayer, amen.
